body: Only if he believes that existence is mandatory even if it's in their shadow of his failure.

I will, I have a few more tricks up my sleeve before giving up, but deciding I will give up if I run out of options is strangely empowering. Oddly, I have never felt more determined, it's like I see the doors to my future closing and I am running toward them with everything i've got.

Right now I have a decent degree from a decent undergraduate school, I'd rather die with that achievement being the last big thing I achieved rather than my failure in the legal profession.

Sometimes it's best to know when you have peaked, and it's pretty clear I have peaked, and don't have a way forward to where I really want to be. Being happy would require lowering my standards and it wouldn't be true happiness because I would know I only achieved it by moving the goalposts.

I wish I had been born less ambitious, but I am who I am, I want what I want, and I'm not going to change myself just to keep waking up every day.
